role.altitude: The recreation and fitness studies teacher keeps lecturing, demonstrating, planning curricula with colleagues, grading open answers and reading the field; writing slides from scratch, compiling evaluation results, marking closed questions by hand and retyping scores and outcomes shrink.
skills_to_grow: Building and tagging an item bank
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who revises each course every term because the evidence is ready.

tasks.short: Plan the lecture schedule, prepare lecture content and slides, find figures and demonstrations, deliver lectures on topics such as anatomy and conditioning theory, answer questions after class, publish slides and answer content mail.

steps.what: Teacher plans the lecture schedule in a spreadsheet
Teacher prepares lecture content and slides on anatomy, therapeutic recreation and conditioning theory

loop.input: The teacher's outline, existing slides and the course textbook chapters.
loop.check: The teacher reads every slide and checks every anatomical and physiological fact against the textbook.
loop.stop: The teacher writes slides by hand when two drafts are wrong.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each lecture adds new topics and examples.

steps.what: Teacher finds figures, videos and movement demonstrations for the lecture
Teacher delivers lectures to undergraduate or graduate students
Teacher answers student questions after the lecture
Teacher uploads the slides to the course page after each lecture
Teacher answers the same lecture content questions several times by mail

tasks.design: Slide updates start from a draft built from the teacher's outline and the textbook, which the teacher checks line by line. Slides in the shared course folder publish to the course page on the lecture date, instead of being uploaded after each lecture. A course forum lets one answer reach every student, instead of the same mail several times. Planning, finding demonstrations, lecturing and answering questions in class stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Slides were written from scratch, uploaded by hand and questions answered one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting from the teacher's own material, scheduled publishing and course forums.
tasks.still_hard: Demonstrating movement and technique, which needs a person.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a squat fault on a student volunteer.

reach.learn: Whether slides are online before the lecture.

evidence.claim: Drafting teaching materials is not among the high-risk education uses; evaluating learning outcomes is.
Slide drafting from a teacher's outline and scheduled publishing in a learning environment are common features.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing and delivering lectures; preparing syllabi and handouts (task 6425) and moderating classroom discussions (task 6429) are sibling tasks.
s2 is priced at 85 because the teacher checks every slide and most lectures reuse existing slides.
s6 saves uploading by hand; s7 saves repeated answers.
Planning, demonstrations, lecturing and questions in class keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of new lectures per year.
research_questions: Are slides online before the lecture more often?

incremental.description: Teacher keeps the course forum tidy.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: repeat courses; high: new courses with many new lectures.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile evaluation results, evaluate the course and decide changes, plan curricula with colleagues, observe teaching methods, revise course content and materials, write the change proposal, retype changes into the course catalogue and exchange versions by mail.

steps.what: Teacher compiles course evaluation results and pass rates into a spreadsheet
Teacher evaluates the course and decides what to revise
Teacher plans curricula with colleagues in programme meetings
Teacher observes and discusses methods of instruction with colleagues
Teacher revises course content and course materials

loop.input: The decided changes, the learning outcomes and the current materials.
loop.output: Draft revised sections and an outcome-to-material table.
loop.check: The teacher reads every revised section; the table must cite a material for each learning outcome.
loop.stop: The teacher revises by hand when two drafts miss the decided changes.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each revision rewrites content for new outcomes.

steps.what: Teacher writes the course change proposal for the programme committee
Teacher retypes changed learning outcomes into the course catalogue system
Teacher mails versions of the revised curriculum to colleagues and merges comments

tasks.design: A course dashboard reads the evaluation system and grade records, showing evaluation results and pass rates per course, instead of results compiled by hand. Colleagues comment in one shared document with tracked changes, instead of mailed versions. Learning outcomes are kept once in the course catalogue and the course document reads from it, instead of being retyped. Revisions start from a draft tied to the decided changes. Evaluating, deciding, planning with colleagues and the proposal stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were compiled by hand and outcomes kept in two places.
tasks.enabler_now: Course dashboards on evaluation and grade data, shared documents and catalogue links.
tasks.still_hard: Small courses where evaluation numbers say little.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a low score reflects the course or the timetable.

ambition.what: Review each course every term instead of only at programme review.

tasks.altitude: Less compiling and retyping; curriculum judgement stays.

evidence.claim: Dashboards able to monitor staff, such as per-examiner marking views, need works council consent.
Grades kept in the learning environment must also be published in the student record system, a double entry.

assumptions: Boundary: planning, evaluating and revising curricula; preparing syllabi and handouts (task 6425) and collaborating on teaching issues (task 6433) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: evaluation and grade data available per course for about 70% of courses; s1 is priced at that share.
The works council consents before course dashboards that show results per teacher are used.
s5 is priced at 85 because every revised section is read; s7 saves retyping; s8 saves merging mailed versions.
Evaluating, deciding, meetings and the proposal keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of courses revised per year.
research_questions: Are courses revised after each evaluation more often?

incremental.description: Teacher reads the course dashboard each term.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small courses with few changes; high: large courses revised each term.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read current literature, search journal sites for new papers, read professional newsletters, talk with colleagues and participate in professional conferences to keep abreast of developments in the field.

steps.what: Teacher searches journal sites for new papers
Teacher reads current literature in the field
Teacher reads professional newsletters and mailing lists
Teacher talks with colleagues about developments
Teacher participates in professional conferences

tasks.design: Saved searches and table-of-contents alerts in a reference manager deliver new papers on the teacher's topics each week, instead of searching journal sites by hand. Reading, newsletters, talking with colleagues and conferences stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: New papers were found by browsing journal sites.
tasks.still_hard: Practice knowledge shared only at conferences.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from a colleague which new training method does not work.

evidence.claim: Reference managers and literature databases offer saved searches and new-issue alerts.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping abreast of the field; conducting research (task 6441) and compiling bibliographies (task 6437) are sibling tasks.
s1 saves browsing for new papers; reading them keeps its full time.
Newsletters, talks and conferences keep their full time.
unknowns: Hours spent on reading per week.
research_questions: Do teachers read more new papers?

incremental.description: Teacher sets up and adjusts saved searches.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: teachers who already use alerts; high: teachers who browse journal sites.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile examination questions, check the exam with a second examiner, brief invigilators and markers, administer the exam, mark closed questions, grade open answers, total scores and compute grades, enter grades, arrange rooms and hold the exam review.

steps.what: Teacher selects and writes items to compile examinations from previous exams
Teacher and a second examiner check the exam against the learning outcomes
Teacher assigns and briefs invigilators and markers
Teacher and invigilators administer examinations in the exam room
Teacher marks closed questions by hand against the key
Teacher grades open answers with the rubric
Teacher types scores into a spreadsheet, totals them and computes grades
Teacher enters grades in the student record system
Teacher arranges exam rooms and special arrangements with the exam office by mail
Teacher holds the exam review session with students

tasks.design: Questions live in an item bank tagged by learning outcome, so the teacher reuses and adapts items and writes new ones, instead of copying from old exam files. Digital exams in the exam system mark closed questions against the key, total the scores and apply the grade formula, instead of marking by hand and typing scores into a spreadsheet; the teacher checks the item analysis. Open answers are graded by the teacher with the rubric, with no model scoring. Checking the exam, briefing, administering, room arrangements and the review session stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Closed questions were marked by hand and scores retyped into spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Item banks and digital exam systems with closed-question marking and item analysis.
tasks.still_hard: Practical exams of movement skills, which are marked live.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a borderline answer shows understanding.
tasks.altitude: Less hand marking and retyping; grading judgement stays.

evidence.claim: An exam tool auto-marks closed questions, splits open ones among markers and gives item statistics.
Evaluating learning outcomes is a high-risk use under annex III point 3, so no model proposes scores here.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results.

assumptions: Boundary: compiling, administering and grading examinations; grading class work and papers (task 6422) and maintaining grade records (task 6423) are sibling tasks.
s8 is part of maintaining grades and required records, which sibling task 6423 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s5 and s7: about 60% of exams are taken in the digital exam system; s5 and s7 are priced at that share.
s1 is priced at 75 because new items are still written for each exam.
Administering, open-answer grading and review sessions keep their full time.
research_questions: Do grades reach students sooner after the exam?

incremental.description: Teacher tags and maintains items in the item bank.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly paper and practical exams; high: digital exams with many closed questions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
